title: StopWatch / StickS3 / Core2 UIFlow2 interface retest

execution.environment: macOS arm64; three isolated Device Service ports/state directories; QEMU virtual device

checks.name: System runtime
checks.details: 50 PASS + 1 STATE_PASS on each of StopWatch, StickS3 and Core2

checks.name: Protocol and owned peers
checks.details: sockets, EasySocket, MQTT, network, EzData and ESP-NOW pass; stock requests2, Modbus async and TLS retain their SDK errors

checks.name: M5UI full matrix
checks.details: 507 observable results, 29 READY frames and zero unobserved methods per StopWatch/Core2; three stock failures retained

checks.name: Core2 BLE NUS
checks.details: two settle-corrected sessions at 8/8; one pre-settle deinit timeout retained as timing control

checks.name: Board hardware probes
checks.details: 115 CALL_OK + 66 API_ASSERTION_PASS + 1 OBSERVED per device; device-local AXP192/IR/IOE/PM1 groups executed

notes: All conclusions are limited to the listed stock firmware, QEMU and virtual runtime profiles.
StopWatch and StickS3 stock internal-controller BLE do not inherit the Core2 native-HCI result.
The BLE 2-second settle addresses a probe race with the stock post-disconnect advertising restart; it does not prove arbitrary active(False) calls always complete promptly.
No open GitHub issue or pull request was present at task completion.
